text:
elena: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change (fallthrough to fused-attn-v2), we're seeing a P99 spike on the long-tail bench for the seq=4096 workload. p50/p95 look fine. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dash/bench/seq4096-kernelcomp
cheng: ugh, saw that in CI alerts at 02:13. p99 jumped from ~190ms -> ~520ms on the nightly harness for the same model + batch mix.
tarun: can you paste the bench command you used? want to reproduce locally.
elena: sure — this is the harness run: 
```
./bench_runner --model llama-13b --seq 4096 --batch 4 --workload=tail --duration=600 --kernels=fused-attn-v2,ref-attn
```
sam: quick hypothesis: the fused-attn-v2 path may have a rare codegen fallback that activates for certain token alignment patterns. I saw similar in an older PR.
cheng: also worth checking KV cache effects — the long-tail harness warms differently because we use random prefixes; may expose memory-pressure cascades.
elena: repro steps: ran the same command on a dev GPU (A100), enabled debug logs for kernel selector. saw a single request that hit a slow fallback path: 
```
[2026-03-18T02:09:45Z] kernel_selector: selected fused-attn-v2
[2026-03-18T02:09:45Z] fused-attn-v2: codegen fallback triggered: matmul-tile-align mismatch -> using generic-kernel
[2026-03-18T02:09:45Z] generic-kernel: backend exec time=482ms
```
ops-bot: CI alert: nightly/long-tail/seq4096 p99 >= 500ms (triggered 3x in last 24h).
tarun: can you share the exact input distribution? Maybe there's a small fraction of requests with odd seq shapes (like 4080 vs 4096) that cause align edges.
elena: harness uses variable prompt prefixes (len 0-512) then generate 3584 tokens. So we do see many different prefix alignments.
cheng: suggestion: add an alignment-normalizer in the selector: round seq to 64-tile boundaries for kernel categorization; if fallback occurs, route to ref-attn earlier. But that hides real perf for true-aligned workloads.
sam: alternative: add telemetry tag for fallback codepath (kernel_name + fallback_reason + seq_shape) so we can quantify how often this happens in prod vs harness. then decide if selector policy needs adjustment.
isha: I can add a quick patch to the harness to collect the fallback_reason counts and emit a CSV; will run overnight.
elena: thanks. also want to rule out regression in scheduler: p99 spike could be head-of-line queuing due to a rare large exec. check instance-level concurrency logs.
cheng: I pulled the instance trace — saw one slot with a 480ms exec that increased queue depth for next 3 small requests -> tail blow-up. trace: https://traces.redwood/trace/0a1b2c
tarun: if it's a single heavy exec, a mitigation is preemptive backpressure or using bounded-concurrency per-kernel. But that's longer-term. For triage, can we reproduce deterministically with a crafted prefix that triggers tile misalignment?
elena: I made one: prefix length 137 triggers fallback 100% in my dev runs. sending to harness now as a focused test.
ops-bot: debug-run queued: nightly-debug/seq4096-fallback-test (job 4872).
sam: if deterministic, patch candidate: modify selector to prefer ref-attn when fallback_reason == "tile-align-mismatch" for sequences in [4090,4096] until we fix codegen. low risk hotfix.
cheng: agree but need a quick risk assessment — that change will slightly change perf for aligned cases (maybe +2-3ms). Should gate with canary on a small fraction.
elena: I'll open an RFC-hotfix PR with canary rollout config and a metric checklist (p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost). tagging tarun & sam for review.
nisha: results from the CSV run: fallback occurrences in harness: 0.7% overall, but concentrated in seeds with prefix_len % 64 in [9..17]. attaching CSV to PR.
elena: next steps: (1) hotfix selector rule + canary, (2) file a follow-up to fix codegen fallback path in fused-attn-v2, (3) add telemetry to product runtime to count fallback reasons. I'll drive 1 & 3 this week.
sam: +1. make sure to add regression test in bench-harness that includes the crafted prefix to prevent future regressions.
tarun: also add a smoke test that runs on deploy: 1000 short-gen requests with mixed prefixes and assert p99 < 250ms.
elena: noted. filing PRs now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
